report.summary: Parsed chunk 1 of slice.py; enumerated public symbols and checkable claims.
risks: estimate_tokens | low | Fallback heuristic (chars//4) may undercount source code, making reduction ratios flattering. Can be settled by ensuring tiktoken is installed or by verifying against actual token counts.

handoff.purpose: Define semantic_slice and its helper functions for assembling a distilled slice of a codebase.

symbols.note: Returns token count using tiktoken if available, else heuristic chars//4.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice`` instead hands it exactly the relevant neighborhood: the FOCUS (a file, or a single symbol) in full; its DEPENDENCIES (what it imports) as signature skeletons — orientation, not full bodies; its CALLERS (who imports it) as skeletons; everything else omitted.
claims.why: The chunk defines helpers but does not show the full assembly logic that creates the slice content; the actual inclusion of dependencies and callers as skeletons is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: ``estimate_tokens``: Token count for the distill ratio. Uses a real BPE tokenizer (tiktoken) when installed, else a ~4-chars/token heuristic — see ``tokens.count_tokens``.
claims.why: The function calls count_tokens(text) which implements that behavior; the docstring accurately describes the function's behavior as seen in the code.

claims.text: ``_whole_repo_tokens``: The distill ratio's DENOMINATOR, plus whether it was actually measured.
claims.why: The function returns (max(1, int(tok)), True) if total_tokens exists, else (max(1, total_chars//4), False); the docstring matches.

claims.text: ``_whole_repo_tokens``: ``total_tokens`` is now carried through the index by the same tokenizer.
claims.why: The claim about how total_tokens is populated in the index is not verifiable from this chunk; it depends on index building code not shown.

claims.text: ``_whole_repo_tokens``: The fallback survives for index dicts that predate the field: an older JSON dump, or the Rust engine (structcore-rs emits total_chars only).
claims.why: The existence of older JSON dumps or Rust engine behavior is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: ``_units_of``: Editable units of a file: code units, or -- for a document -- SECTIONS.
claims.why: The code checks if doc_spec_for(rel) is not None and returns markdown_mod.parse_document sections; otherwise uses spec_for and extract_units for code units.

claims.text: ``_units_of``: A ``DocSection`` is field-compatible with a ``CodeUnit`` (module/name/line/ end_line/loc/source/language), so a caller that already handles units needs no type switch.
claims.why: The chunk does not define DocSection or CodeUnit; compatibility cannot be verified.

claims.text: ``_units_of``: What a caller MUST NOT do is feed sections into the call-graph approximation: identifiers in prose are not calls, and ``semantic_slice`` keeps the two apart for that reason.
claims.why: The chunk does not show how sections are used in call-graph approximation; this claim is about usage outside this function.

claims.text: ``_skeleton``: Signature-level digest of a file: one line per unit (its first line).
claims.why: The code iterates over units and for each unit extracts the first non-empty line (first) and formats it as a line with location info.

claims.text: ``_skeleton``: For a DOCUMENT the analogue is exact and is delegated to ``markdown.document_skeleton``: the heading tree is the signature set, the prose is the body, the body is dropped, and the drop is reported inline.
claims.why: The function calls markdown_mod.document_skeleton but the implementation of that function is not in this chunk; the claim about its behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: ``_skeleton``: The result is never larger than the raw document.
claims.why: Not verifiable from this chunk; depends on markdown.document_skeleton implementation.

claims.text: ``_skeleton``: The old fallthrough (``spec_for`` returns None for .md, so zero units, so the ``len(out) == 1`` branch) emitted twelve raw lines of prose under a header reading ``(skeleton)`` — presenting a document as though it had signatures, with no statement that the other 3,580 lines existed at all.
claims.why: The current code explicitly checks doc_spec_for before spec_for, so the fallthrough for .md files no longer occurs; the old behavior is fixed by the new routing.

claims.text: ``_reverse_edges``: Callers map: rel -> the rels that import it.
claims.why: The function returns a dict mapping target to list of sources; the code builds this from import_edges_reverse or computes it from import_edges.

claims.text: ``_reverse_edges``: ``build_index`` ships this precomputed as ``import_edges_reverse`` because it is index-invariant and this function is on the per-target path: the eval harness and the web API both call ``semantic_slice`` in a loop against ONE shared index, so inverting the forward map here would repeat the same O(E) work per call.
claims.why: The claim about build_index precomputation and usage patterns is not verifiable from this chunk; it depends on other parts of the codebase.

claims.text: ``_reverse_edges``: The fallback below exists only for an index dict that predates the key (an older JSON dump); it iterates ``sorted()`` so the appended caller lists come out in the same order as the precomputed ones.
claims.why: The code falls back to building from import_edges with sorted(src) and setdefault; the order of appended callers is determined by sorted(edges) iteration.

claims.text: ``_assemble_slice``: Join FOCUS + kept neighbour units (each under its section header, in emission order) + the WITHHELD block + an optional TRIMMED marker.
claims.why: The code builds out list starting with focus_block, then iterates neighbors adding section headers and texts, then extends with withheld_lines and optionally appends trimmed_marker.

claims.text: ``_assemble_slice``: A section header is emitted once, and only for a section that still has a kept unit — so dropping every unit of a section drops its header too.
claims.why: The code tracks last_section and only appends section header when it changes; if no units remain for a section, its header is never added.

claims.text: ``_assemble_slice``: With the full neighbour list and no marker this reproduces the old flat join byte-for-byte (the un-budgeted path is unchanged).
claims.why: Cannot verify what the 'old flat join' was; this claim refers to behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``_fit_budget``: Degrade an over-budget slice by dropping WHOLE neighbour units — never string-truncating — until it fits ``budget`` tokens. FOCUS and the WITHHELD block are always kept (a tail truncation would silently delete the anti-hallucination breadcrumb, the exact failure the gate prevents).
claims.why: The loop drops entire neighbor units (pop from kept), and the marker is added only after dropping; focus_block and withheld_lines are always included in _assemble_slice call.

claims.text: ``_fit_budget``: Lowest keep-priority goes first (callers/signatures before dependency and callee bodies); within a tier the later-emitted unit goes first, so the earliest / most-relevant neighbour survives longest.
claims.why: The selection of victim uses kept[i]['keep'] and -i, but the ordering of 'keep' values and how they correspond to 'callers/signatures before dependency and callee bodies' is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``_fit_budget``: The TRIMMED marker's own cost is counted each pass so the kept set fits WITH the marker present.
claims.why: The marker string is constructed before the estimate_tokens check and includes the current dropped count; the estimate_tokens call includes the marker in the assembled slice.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: Assemble a semantic slice of ``target``.
claims.why: The function body begins assembling the slice: resolves target, reads file, applies egress rule.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: ``lane`` selects the egress gate applied to every file that contributes text to ``slice_text`` (see ``sensitivity.slice_egress_rule``).
claims.why: The import of slice_egress_rule is present but its implementation is not in this chunk; the claim about its behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: ``"trusted"`` (default) — Claude, local Ollama, the eval harness, the local web distill view. The unconditional SECRET FLOOR still runs (a private key never enters a slice, even locally); the default-deny allow-list does NOT, so ordinary source is never withheld here. This is what keeps eval recall at 100%.
claims.why: The behavior of slice_egress_rule for different lanes is not implemented in this chunk; only the call to slice_egress_rule is shown.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: ``"untrusted"`` — a genuinely untrusted external provider (DeepSeek). Floor + the existing default-deny allow-list both apply.
claims.why: Same as above; lane-specific behavior not visible.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: Withholding is REPORTED, never silent: the result gains a sorted ``withheld`` block (path, role, rule) AND an inline ``# ===== WITHHELD ... =====`` breadcrumb in ``slice_text`` so the consuming model sees the gap rather than hallucinating the missing callee. If the FOCUS file itself is denied the slice fails closed — no neighbour slice is returned in its place.
claims.why: The chunk ends before the full implementation; only the focus gate is partially shown. The reporting of withheld and fail-closed behavior is not fully visible.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: ``reduction_pct`` is ``1 - slice_tokens / whole_repo_tokens``. Both sides are now counted by the SAME tokenizer (``tokens.count_tokens``: tiktoken cl100k_base when installed, chars/4 otherwise); the denominator used to be a bare ``total_chars // 4`` regardless, so the ratio mixed a measured numerator with an estimated denominator. ``whole_repo_tokens_exact`` is False when that old estimate is still in play (an index dict lacking ``total_tokens`` -- an older JSON dump, or the Rust engine).
claims.why: The actual computation of reduction_pct and whole_repo_tokens_exact is not shown in this chunk; only _whole_repo_tokens helper is defined.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: ``whole_repo_tokens`` is the summed token count of the IN-CENTER source files -- exactly the file set ``index`` accumulates inside its metric-withholding guard, so .daedalusignore'd and out-of-scope files are excluded from the baseline just as they are from the slice.
claims.why: The index building and its metric-withholding guard are not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: It is deliberately NOT identical to what ``eval/harness.py:_whole_repo_text`` concatenates for the Tier-2 A/B, which differs in three ways: it prepends a ``# ===== rel =====`` header per file (so its total runs HIGHER), it truncates at a char cap (so on a large repo its total runs LOWER, and it reports ``b_truncated``), and it walks the filesystem with its own ignore-dir list rather than the index's scope, so the two can disagree about which files "the repo" contains. Treat ``reduction_pct`` as the index-scoped ratio and Tier-2's ``tokens_B`` as the as-fed-to-a-model count; they answer different questions and should not be expected to match.
claims.why: This claim refers to code in eval/harness.py which is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: ``max_tokens`` (default ``None`` -> no cap, byte-identical to before) caps the assembled ``slice_text``. When exceeded the slice degrades by dropping WHOLE neighbour units (never truncating text), always keeping the FOCUS and the WITHHELD block and appending a visible ``# ===== CONTEXT TRIMMED ... =====`` marker; ``trimmed_count`` reports how many neighbours were dropped.
claims.why: The actual handling of max_tokens and the call to _fit_budget are not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: ``semantic_slice``: ``include_focus`` (default ``True`` -> byte-identical to before) controls only whether the FOCUS file's BODY is emitted into ``slice_text``. With ``False`` the body is replaced by a one-line header and ``included[0]`` is reported as ``mode="omitted"``; the focus source is still read and still drives symbol resolution (callees/callers). The offload rewrite path sets this: it already puts the file body in the prompt separately, so duplicating it via the FOCUS block would waste the window -- the slice then contributes only neighbour context. INVARIANT: the FOCUS GATE (the floor scan of the FULL focus text and its fail-closed refusal) runs FIRST and IDENTICALLY in both modes -- omitting the body never skips the gate, so a secret-bearing focus is refused either way.
claims.why: The handling of include_focus is not implemented in this chunk; only the focus gate (reading and egress rule) is partially shown.

observations.what: The chunk ends abruptly mid-function, likely at the point where focus_rule is computed and a breadcrumb is started.
The docstring of _whole_repo_tokens contains a historical note about a bug where the denominator was chars//4, but this is now fixed; the function returns exact flag.
The docstring of _skeleton explicitly claims the old fallthrough for .md files is now fixed by routing to document_skeleton; the code confirms this.
The docstring of semantic_slice makes many claims about behavior that is not implemented in this chunk; the actual implementation is only partially visible.
